# 2007 CS Q78: Which string is generated by the grammar

## Question

**Statement for Linked Answer Questions 78 & 79.** Consider the CFG with $\lbrace S, A, B \rbrace$ as the non-terminal alphabet, $\lbrace a, b \rbrace$ as the terminal alphabet, $S$ as the start symbol and the following set of production rules:

$$S \to aB \qquad S \to bA$$
$$B \to b \qquad A \to a$$
$$B \to bS \qquad A \to aS$$
$$B \to aBB \qquad A \to bAA$$

**Q.78** Which of the following strings is generated by the grammar?

- (A) aaaabb
- (B) aabbbb
- (C) aabbab
- (D) abbbba

<details class="success" markdown="1">
<summary>Answer</summary>

**C**

</details>

<details class="info" markdown="1">
<summary>Solution</summary>

This grammar generates the non-empty strings with **equally many $a$s and $b$s** (from $S$: $B$ derives strings with one extra $b$, $A$ strings with one extra $a$).

(A) has 4 $a$s and 2 $b$s, (B) has 2 and 4, (D) has 2 and 4. Only (C) $aabbab$ has three $a$s and three $b$s, and it can be derived:
$$S \Rightarrow aB \Rightarrow aaBB \Rightarrow aabB \Rightarrow aabbS \Rightarrow aabbaB \Rightarrow aabbab.$$

So (C).

- (A), (B) and (D) have unequal numbers of $a$s and $b$s, so no derivation exists.

**Code check:** Python CYK-style parse-tree counter: $aabbab$ has 2 parse trees; $aaaabb$, $aabbbb$ and $abbbba$ have 0. Also, for all strings of length up to 12 the grammar generates a string if and only if it has equally many $a$s and $b$s (0 exceptions either way).

**Status note:** `unverified`. GATE 2007 had no official answer key, so there is nothing to compare against. This is my own answer.

**Key idea:** the grammar generates exactly the strings with equal numbers of $a$ and $b$; check the count of each letter first.

</details>
